paragraphs: Rabbi Uziel, son of Rabbi Nehunya, of Berat Havran [printed: דברת חוורן].

Hyman cites the end of [Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 1:7](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Shabbat.1.7.3) and the supplied Beitzah locator ל״ג ה״ב [compare [3:2](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Beitzah.3.2.3)] for Rabbi Chizkiyah reporting in Uziel’s name. In [Maaser Sheni](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Maaser_Sheni.5.1.6), Hyman says, the text mistakenly reads R’ Yechezkel. [Moed Katan 5a](https://www.sefaria.org/Moed_Katan.5a.16) gives the teaching in the name of R’ Uziel, grandson of R’ Uziel the Elder.

notes.text: [Heilprin’s entry on Uziel son of Nechunya](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=2837&lang=en) also cites Shabbat 1:7 and Beitzah 3:2. In the consulted Shabbat and Beitzah, Chizkiyah and Uziel appear side by side. Hyman presents the relationship as a transmission from Uziel.

The linked Bavli gives a parallel grave-marking teaching from a grandson of Uziel the Elder. [Heilprin’s corresponding notice](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=2838&lang=en) cites that grandson wording as well. These references leave the relationship between the two Uziel notices open.

The consulted Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 1:7 joins Chizkiyah and Uziel with “and,” while Beitzah 3:2 puts their names side by side. Both call Uziel the son of Chunya of Berat Chavran. In Maaser Sheni 5:1, the Guggenheimer text has Chizkiyah, while the Vilna-based text published by Daat has Yechezkel. Both put the named sage beside Uziel and give the teaching in Chunya’s name. Daat’s wording explicitly has them speak together. The judgment that Yechezkel is an error is Hyman’s. Bavli Moed Katan 5a attributes the parallel grave-marking teaching to Uziel, grandson of Uziel the Elder.
